extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, university students, technical educators, and practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Announcements, society reports, course details, prizes, and institutional notices relating to university and technical education and scientific societies, intended to inform scientists, students, and administrators. Includes procedural details (attendance, admissions), contest/prize conditions, and standards for museum/exam-oriented materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance requirement for physical department students
rubrics_metrics.description: In the physical department, all students are required to attend both the lecture and the laboratory course in each class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as a rule for course participation — lecture+laboratory attendance is mandatory for satisfactory progress in physical department subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent attendance for electrical engineering students lacking prior electrical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Students of electrical engineering must attend classes in electricity and magnetism concurrently if they have no knowledge of the principles of electrical science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent enrollment in foundational classes is required to ensure adequate grounding; used as a condition for enrollment in electrical engineering curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and duration of systematic technical courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic courses of study extending over three or more years are arranged in various branches of technology; the time-tables of these courses should be useful as a guide to serious students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice/standard about curricular design for technical education: multi-year structured courses with published timetables intended to guide committed students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial-aid admission policy (Woolwich Polytechnic governors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The governors are desirous that no young man or woman shall be deprived of the advantages of the instruction given in the polytechnic on the ground of inability to pay the fees. The principal is authorised to admit students free who desire to attend any of the classes and to work steadily, but are unable to pay the necessary fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional policy standard for equitable access — students demonstrating willingness to work steadily may be admitted without fees if unable to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay prize conditions (Association of Technical Institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Accommodation of Technical Institutions offers two prizes, each of £25, for the two best essays, one on 'The Bearing of Technical Education on Industrial Progress,' and the other on 'The Bearing of Technical Education on Agriculture and on Industries of a Rural Character.' Particulars of the conditions may be obtained from Dr. Clav, Northern Polytechnic, Holloway, London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines contest topics and prize amounts; further submission conditions and judging criteria are available from the named contact — implies essays judged for best treatment of the specified topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission criteria for public lecture course (Dr. W. M. Bayliss)
rubrics_metrics.description: A course of eight lectures on 'Certain Fundamental Problems in Physiology common to Animals and Plants' will be given by Dr. W. M. Bayliss at University College (University of London). The lectures are open to all students of the University of London; also to qualified medical men and to such other persons as are specially admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets permitted audience categories (university students, qualified medical men, specially admitted persons) — an admission standard for continuing-education lectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for museum donations/cataloguing (University museum gift)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prof. W. C. McIntosh presented the University museum with 3150 spirit preparations comprising: (1) a named series (about 1150) illustrating the marine zoology of St. Andrews — the types of 'Invertebrate Marine Fauna and Fishes' (1875); (2) a glazed cabinet illustrating development and life-history of the salmon of the Tay in ninety-five preparations; (3) a reference series (265) from trawling expeditions of 1884, each station showing both fishes and invertebrates; (4) a general zoological collection in spirit (about 1595 specimens) chiefly marine; (5) forty-five typical botanical preparations including pitcher plants with their insects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied standards for a university collection: include named/type series, developmental/life-history series, station-referenced reference series with provenance data, broad general collections, and representative botanical preparations — importance of detailed cataloguing and variety of specimen types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen-based reporting standard for occurrence records
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary record of the occurrence of Chlamydoselachus in New South Wales was based upon portions of a specimen cast ashore comprising the skull and about 1½ vertebræ; the specimen measured over 10 feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied standard for species occurrence reports: base records on physical specimens (with identifiable parts and measurements) and provide measurements and provenance information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination-aligned teaching materials (microscopic slides)
rubrics_metrics.description: Botanic microscopical slides (sold in series) are adapted for Board of Education and London University Examinations, illustrating root, stem, leaf, pollen tubes, flower development, embryo structures, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational material should be tailored to examination syllabuses by including illustrative specimens that map to listed topics; series composition and labeling intended to satisfy exam requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and editorial submission addresses and differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements and business letters for Nature should be addressed to the Publisher; contributions to the Editor. The telegraphic address of Nature is 'PHUSIS', LONDON.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural standard for where to send different kinds of communications: business/ads -> Publisher; editorial/contributions -> Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges and format specifications for advertisements in Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified rates: Quarter page at half, per line charges, one-sixth page/eighth column rates, columns, half page, whole page rates are listed (e.g., One column 11s 6d; Half Page or a Column 3s 6d; Whole Page 8s). The first line in heavy type charged as two lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers must follow prescribed size/rate structure and typographic charging rules when submitting adverts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription pricing and frequency options for Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscription rates given: Yearly, Half-yearly, Quarterly with different prices for the British Isles and for all places abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized pricing structure for subscription management; subscribers choose frequency and territory determines rate.
